title: The Khalsa Predates Abdali and Holds a Legitimate Claim

blocks.text: This page rejects the Mughal attempt to dismiss Sikh power as a recent accident of invasion. The author insists that the Khalsa Panth existed at the time of Aurangzeb, and that such a presence could no more be concealed than the sun behind passing clouds.

He then grounds Sikh authority in sacrifice and inheritance. The Gurus had surrendered their lives, Five provinces had been taken away through persecution and fraud, and therefore the Sikhs had a legitimate claim to the land they were now defending.

The argument is presented not merely as sectarian feeling but as a case tested before an outside listener. Captain David Murray is made to hear the account in full and to accept that Perfectly legitimate was the Sikhs claim indeed.
